results.reason: Identifies the §2.2 automatic renewal for successive five-year periods and the 270/240-day notice window. Calculates the window as October 3 to November 2, 2026, notes lock-in to June 30, 2032 with escalating commitments, and recommends a protective non-renewal notice before the deadline.

Does not mention the §5.3 30-day objection or removal right, the roughly September 20, 2026 deadline, or deemed acceptance. It treats the notice only as formally compliant and offers commercial steps.

Explains that the §11.1 indemnity has no fault qualifier and covers Brightmere-caused claims, that §12.3(a) excludes it from the cap, and that the §11.2 indemnity stays capped. Recommends narrowing to Halvorsen's own fault and making it mutual or capped.

Identifies that First Amendment §3 deletes and replaces §12.3 and drops the recall carve-out. Explains recall reimbursement is now subject to the 12-month fees cap, which a large recall could exceed, and recommends reinstatement.

Identifies First Amendment §6.1–6.2 (Delaware law, Wilmington courts) as conflicting with D1 §17.1–17.2 (New York law, New York County), notes the amendment prevails under §1.4, and recommends restoring New York.
States the Initial Term ends June 30, 2027.
States that under D1 §1.4 written amendments prevail over the body of the Agreement.
Formatted as a memorandum to the Supervising Partner. Each issue has 'Where', 'Why it matters for Halvorsen', and 'Recommended fix' sections.
Concludes that recall reimbursement is now capped.
Expressly acknowledges that the First Amendment's Delaware provisions now govern.
